title: OpenAI-compat: invoke choice telemetry and message sanitizer
author: Priya Kapur
description: Context: customers consuming OpenAI-compatible function/tool calling reported two recurring problems: (1) ambiguous tool selection metadata in the compatibility layer made attribution and fallback reasoning lossy; (2) streaming fragments from tools occasionally omitted consistent message typing which broke downstream stream reassembly and structured output validation. This PR introduces a non-breaking compatibility shim that preserves deterministic selection rationale and enforces a sanitized tool message envelope for streaming clients. Changes: add an 'invoke_metadata' header for every tool-invoke that records selection_reason (explicit|heuristic|fallback), selection_score (rounded float), and source_model_hint. Ensure this metadata is preserved in the OpenAI-compatible function_call/choices mapping for auditability. Normalize streaming fragments to include fragment_id, role:"tool", name, and a message_type tag (result|error|progress). Implement a message sanitizer that strips unsafe top-level keys, maps legacy tool args -> params, and emits structured validation failures to telemetry instead of rejecting the stream. The compatibility adapter preserves the original tool schema in a compressed provenance blob so consumers can opt-in to strict schema checks. Backwards compatibility: the adapter keeps the original API surface for existing clients; all new fields are optional and guarded by feature flags. Testing & rollout: unit tests added for serializer/deserializer, stream-fragment reassembly tests, and an end-to-end integration with the streaming test harness. Feature-flagged rollout to 10% of traffic with an A/B canary and automatic rollback on _structured-output-regressions_ alert. Checklist: [x] design doc linked (Linear ENG-1203) [x] unit tests [x] integration tests [x] canary config [x] telemetry dashboards updated. Motivation: this reduces silent tool-selection ambiguity, improves stream stability for long-running tool outputs, and gives SREs and product teams deterministic telemetry to diagnose quality regressions.

feat(adapter): preserve provenance blob and map to OpenAI function_call metadata
fix(stream): enforce fragment_id and role/name typing in stream frames
chore(tests): add stream reassembly and schema-fuzz cases
docs: document compatibility flags and rollback procedure

runtime/stream/framer.go +45 -8: Require fragment_id and enforce role=="tool" when source == tool, include message_type field
api/openai_adapter.py +110 -30: Map InvokeMetadata into choices[].metadata and keep original schema in compressed provenance key
review_comments: Evan Morris: Can we guarantee selection_score rounding is stable across language runtimes? If not it will make offline diffs noisy.
Priya Kapur (author): We quantize to two decimal places and store the raw float in the provenance blob for auditability; added unit test to assert stable rounding across go/python adapters.
Lina Torres: The sanitizer looks good but we need a short-circuit for high-throughput tool outputs to avoid CPU pressure. Consider a fast-path that only tags message_type without full sanitization.
Priya Kapur (author): Added a 'fast_sanitize' opt-in flag in the framer that bypasses deep sanitization for high-throughput canaries; default remains full-sanitize.
Omar Haddad: Please add an alert for 'stream-reassembly-failure-rate' and include the dashboard link in release notes.
Priya Kapur (author): Alert added and dashboards updated; link included in release notes.
discussion_summary: Team agreed on non-breaking opt-in fields and a compressed provenance approach to preserve original schema without forcing schema changes on existing consumers.
Performance concerns were addressed with a fast_sanitize opt-in; SRE will monitor CPU at 10% canary before widening rollout.
Telemetry schema version bumped to v2 for invoke events.
Docs and runbook updated to include rollback steps and alert runbook for structured-output regressions.
release_notes: Improves OpenAI-compatible function/tool invocation stability: preserves selection rationale, sanitizes streaming tool messages, and adds optional provenance for audit/debug. Rollout is feature-flagged; see docs/openai-compat/invoke-metadata.md for migration steps and observability links.
